papers.title: Oculomotor and Cognitive Correlates of White Matter Organization in Military Personnel with Chronic Mild, Moderate, and Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.reason: The study links oculomotor and cognitive measures with white-matter organization across traumatic brain injury severities, providing a relevant multimodal assessment framework.

papers.title: Before the task begins: linking resting-state gamma oscillations to face-name associative memory
papers.reason: Resting-state EEG gamma power predicts associative-memory retrieval, but the study does not directly address executive function or working-memory processes.

papers.title: Altered neurovascular coupling in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease: Associations with polysomnography-derived sleep parameters and cognition.
papers.reason: The paper examines neural physiology, sleep, and cognition in cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease without an evident focus on executive-function mechanisms.

papers.title: Association between Toxocara spp. seropositivity and cognitive outcomes in older adults: a cross-sectional analysis of the amirkola health and ageing project.
papers.reason: This epidemiological association study concerns general cognitive outcomes in older adults rather than executive-function modelling or digital assessment.

papers.title: Evidence Consistent with Accelerated Inhibitory Build-up Following Stronger Subliminal Motor Activation: An EEG Trajectory-Fitting Analysis.
papers.reason: EEG trajectory fitting, midfrontal theta, and drift-rate modelling directly characterize the dynamics of inhibitory cognitive control.

papers.title: Peripheral hearing, brainstem auditory responses, and P300 potentials in Parkinson's disease: A cross-sectional study with one-year follow-up.
papers.reason: Auditory P300 measurements provide electrophysiological evidence about sensory-cognitive processing in Parkinson's disease, although executive function is not specifically examined.

papers.title: The role of gender in informant reports of cognitive decline in the United States and Mexico.
papers.reason: The study identifies demographic and cultural biases in informant-based cognitive assessment but does not investigate executive function or digital biomarkers.

papers.title: Altered microstructure in end-stage renal disease patients with maintenance hemodialysis: A diffusion kurtosis imaging analysis.
papers.reason: Diffusion imaging and support-vector regression are used to predict general MoCA performance, but no executive-function-specific construct or digital behavioural measure is studied.

papers.title: Effect of N-Acetylcysteine in Reducing Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction after Anaesthesia in Elderly Patients Undergoing Day Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Study.
papers.reason: The trial evaluates prevention of general postoperative cognitive dysfunction rather than modelling, neural mechanisms, or digital assessment of executive function.
